entries.meaning: Of Dutch origin, from Middle Dutch Diederic, from Old Dutch *Thiodarīk, from Frankish *Theodarīk, ultimately from Proto-Germanic *Þeudarīks. Compare with Derek, Theodoric.
entries.note: A male given name from Dutch.

entries.meaning: From Irish Deirdre.
entries.note: A female given name from Irish, variant of Deirdre.

entries.meaning: Borrowed from Spanish Diego, from an Iberian Didacus, of uncertain origin.
entries.note: A male given name from Spanish Diego.

entries.meaning: From Hindi, dirgh (long) + Anta (end) = horizon.
entries.note: A male given name from India, of Indian (particularly Assamese) usage.

entries.meaning: From Old English dīc (“dyke”) + Old Norse býr (“settlement”). The town in Nova Scotia is named after admiral Robert Digby (1732 - 1815).
entries.note: A male given name transferred from the surname.

entries.meaning: From a medieval diminutive of Dick.
entries.note: A surname transferred from the given name.

entries.meaning: (surname): From a medieval diminutive of Dick. : (place name): From Old English degle, ("valley").
entries.note: A surname transferred from the given name.

entries.meaning: Borrowed from Sanskrit दीक्षा (dīkṣā).
entries.note: A female given name from Sanskrit used in India.

entries.meaning: Variation of Dylan, originally from Welsh.
entries.note: A male given name.

entries.meaning: Variant of Dylan.
entries.note: A male given name.

entries.meaning: From the Irish surname, from Breton Leon and Norman Léon, named after Sir Henry de Leon of the Viscounty of Léon. Related to the surname Lyon. Unrelated to the name Dylan, although the homophony may result in the two being considered variant spellings of the same name.
entries.note: A male given name transferred from the surname.

entries.meaning: Transliteration of Sinhalese දිල්රුක්ෂි (dilrukṣi).
entries.note: A transliteration of the Sinhalese female given name දිල්රුක්ෂි (dilrukṣi).

entries.meaning: From Bashkir.
entries.note: A male given name (from Bashkir Дим) .

entries.meaning: From Russian Ди́ма (Díma), a diminutive of the male given name Дми́трий (Dmítrij, “Demetrius”).
entries.note: A transliteration of the Russian male given name diminutive Ди́ма (Díma).

entries.meaning: Transliteration of Greek Δήμητρα (Dímitra), a female given name used in modern Greece.
entries.note: A transliteration of the Greek female given name Δήμητρα (Dímitra).

entries.meaning: Transliteration of Greek Δημήτρης (Dimítris), a male given name used in (modern) Greece. Doublet of Demetrius.
entries.note: A transliteration of the Greek male given name Δημήτρης (Dimítris).

entries.meaning: The given name is apparently from the name of the light cotton fabric, dimity. However, since it is found primarily as an Irish name, it may have originated as a feminine equivalent of Dermot.
entries.note: A female given name of modern usage.

entries.meaning: Borrowed clipping of longer names in many languages, such as Italian Dina.
entries.note: A female given name from Italian.

entries.meaning: From Hebrew דִּינָה (dīna, "judged, vindicated"); see דין.
entries.note: A female given name from Hebrew of biblical origin. Alternative form of Dina.

entries.meaning: Borrowed from Italian Dino.
entries.note: A male given name from Italian, feminine equivalent Dina.

entries.meaning: From Ancient Greek Διοκλῆς (Dioklês)
entries.note: A male given name of historical usage.

entries.meaning: From Latin Diogenēs, from Ancient Greek Διογένης (Diogénēs).
entries.note: A transliteration of the Ancient Greek male given name Διογένης (Diogénēs).

entries.meaning: Borrowed from Ancient Greek Δίων (Díōn). Also a medieval English and French diminutive of Dionysius (Dennis).
entries.note: A male given name from Ancient Greek.

entries.meaning: From Latin Diōnē (“of Jupiter”), from Ancient Greek Διώνη (Diṓnē, “of Zeus”).
entries.note: A female given name from Ancient Greek.

entries.meaning: * (surname): From French Dionne * (given name): From Latin Dione, from Ancient Greek Διώνη (Diṓnē)
entries.note: A female given name from Ancient Greek, variant of Dione.

entries.meaning: Learned borrowing from Latin Dionȳsia, feminine of Dionȳsius, from Ancient Greek Δῐονῡ́σῐος (Dĭonū́sĭos), from Διόνῡσος (Diónūsos, “Dionysus”) + -ῐος (-ĭos, “pertaining to”). Doublet of Denise.
entries.note: A female given name from Latin [in turn from Ancient Greek], masculine equivalent Dionysius.

entries.meaning: From Latin Dionysius, from Ancient Greek Διονύσιος (Dionúsios).
entries.note: A transliteration of the Ancient Greek male given name Διονύσιος (Dionúsios).

entries.meaning: From Hindi दीपा (dīpā), from Sanskrit दीपा (dīpā).
entries.note: A female given name from South Asia.

entries.meaning: Transliteration of Bengali দীপাঞ্জন (dipanjôn).
entries.note: A male given name from Sanskrit.

entries.meaning: Transliteration of Bengali দীপঙ্কর (dipoṅkor).
entries.note: A male given name from Sanskrit.

entries.meaning: Transliteration of Bengali দীপান্বিতা (dipannita).
entries.note: A female given name from Sanskrit.

entries.meaning: From India.
entries.note: A male given name from India, a nickname in India.

entries.meaning: Borrowed from Dutch and North German Dirk.

entries.meaning: Borrowed from Sanskrit दिशा (diśā).
entries.note: A female given name from Sanskrit used in India.

entries.meaning: Borrowed from Sanskrit दिति (diti, “cutting, splitting, dividing”).
entries.note: A female given name from Sanskrit

entries.meaning: Borrowed from Sanskrit दिवाकर (divākara, “Sun”).
entries.note: A male given name from Sanskrit used in India.

entries.meaning: From Sanskrit दिव्या (divyā́), feminine of दिव्य (divyá, “divine, heavenly”).
entries.note: A female given name from Sanskrit.

entries.meaning: Borrowed from Sanskrit दिव्या (divyā́), feminine of दिव्य (divyá, “divine, charming, heavenly”).
entries.note: A female given name from Sanskrit.

entries.meaning: Borrowed from Sanskrit दिव्यांगना (divyāṃganā).
entries.note: A female given name from Sanskrit used in India.

entries.meaning: Borrowed from Sanskrit दिव्यांशु (divyāṃśu, “Sun”).
entries.note: A male given name from Sanskrit used in India.

entries.meaning: Borrowed from Sanskrit दिव्यता (divyatā).

entries.meaning: From Sanskrit दिव्येन्दु (divyendu, “divine moon”). Doublet of Dibyendu.
entries.note: A male given name.

entries.meaning: Borrowed from Sanskrit दिवाकर (divākara, “Sun”).
entries.note: A male given name from Sanskrit used in India.

entries.meaning: From a medieval diminutive of Dick.
entries.note: A surname transferred from the given name.

entries.meaning: First attested in 1859. Unknown, but may come from the Mason-Dixon line, the boundary between the northern states and the southern states, or from the slang term dixie for a Louisiana $10 bill (equivalent to English tenner), in turn from French dix (ten).
entries.note: A female given name transferred from the place name.

entries.meaning: Borrowed from Sanskrit दिया (diyā, “earthen lamp”).
entries.note: A female given name from Sanskrit used in India.

entries.meaning: From Hebrew [Term?].
entries.note: A female given name from Hebrew.

entries.meaning: Reported to be the first person singular of a Romani verb meaning "to awake" (cf. Baltic Romani džangavel, Carpathian Romani žangaul, Sinte Romani džangel, etc.) Could also be a Wallonian version or diminutive of French Jean.
entries.note: A male given name

entries.meaning: Borrowed from Arabic جِبْرِيل (jibrīl).
entries.note: A male given name from Arabic.

entries.meaning: From Russian Дми́трий (Dmítrij), from Byzantine Greek Δημήτριος (Dēmḗtrios), from Δημήτηρ (Dēmḗtēr, “Demeter”) + -ιος (-ios, “pertaining to”). Doublet of Demetrius, Dimitri, and Dimitris.
entries.note: A transliteration of the Russian male given name Дми́трий (Dmítrij).

entries.meaning: From Byzantine Greek Δημήτριος (Dēmḗtrios), from Δημήτηρ (Dēmḗtēr, “Demeter”). Doublet of Demetrius and Dimitris.
entries.note: A transliteration of the Ukrainian male given name Дмитро (Dmytro)

entries.meaning: Regional form of Joan.
entries.note: A female given name.

entries.meaning: From Dobbie.
entries.note: A male given name.

entries.meaning: From a medieval diminutive form of the given name Robert.
entries.note: A locality in the Rural City of Ararat, central western Victoria, Australia

entries.meaning: * As an English surname, possibly from the noun duck. * As a Norwegian surname, from Old Norse dǫkk (“pit, depression”), from Proto-Germanic *dankwaz (“dark”). * As a German surname, spelling variant of Docke, related to the noun Tuch (“cloth, piece of fabric”).
entries.note: A male given name or nickname.

entries.meaning: From a medieval diminutive of Dodge, from the given name Roger.

entries.meaning: From a medieval diminutive of Dodge, from the given name Roger.

entries.meaning: From Dodge + -son and from Dodd + -son.

entries.meaning: * As a south German surname, from toll (“mad, foolish”). * Also as a German surname, spelling variant of Thiel. * As an English surname, from the adjective dull, cognate with the first German derivation. Also compare Dill.

entries.meaning: Borrowed from Spanish Dolores.

entries.meaning: Shortenings.

entries.meaning: Borrowed from Irish Domhnall. Doublet of Donald.
entries.note: A male given name from Irish.

entries.meaning: From Late Latin Dominicus, derived from Dominus (“Lord”).
entries.note: A male given name from Latin, best known for the Spanish saint who founded the Dominican order.

entries.meaning: From French Dominique. Doublet of Dominic.
entries.note: A female given name from French.

entries.meaning: Name of Scottish kings and an early saint, from Scottish Gaelic Dòmhnall and reinforced by Medieval Latin Donvaldus ~ Donaldus, from Old Irish Domnall, from Proto-Celtic *Dubnowalos (“prince / chief of the world”). Doublet of Domhnall.
entries.note: A male given name from Scottish Gaelic.

entries.meaning: A variant of Duncan.
entries.note: A surname transferred from the given name.

entries.meaning: A 19th-century invention from the Italian noun donna; also interpreted as a feminine form of Donald.
entries.note: A female given name from Italian.

entries.meaning: Possibly from Donna + -etta.
entries.note: A female given name originating as a coinage.

entries.meaning: Possibly from Donna + -ette.
entries.note: A female given name originating as a coinage.

entries.meaning: Diminutives + -ie.

entries.meaning: Diminutive forms with -y.
entries.note: A diminutive of the male given names Don, Donald, Donovan, and Adonis.

entries.meaning: From Irish Ó Donndubháin (“descendant of (a person named) brown & black”), from donn (“brown”) and dubh (“black”).
entries.note: A male given name transferred from the surname.

entries.meaning: Blend of Donte + Octavius, the latter revised to accord with -ious.

entries.meaning: Variant of Dougie
entries.note: A diminutive of the male given name Douglas, variant of Dougie

entries.meaning: A diminutive of Dorothy used since early 19th century. Sometimes also short for Theodora or Isidora.
entries.note: A female given name from Ancient Greek.

entries.meaning: From Ancient Greek Δορκάς (Dorkás, “gazelle”), translation of Tabitha in the Bible.
entries.note: A female given name from Ancient Greek of biblical origin.

entries.meaning: Borrowed from Irish and Scottish Gaelic Dorcha (literally “dark”).
entries.note: A female given name from Scottish Gaelic.

entries.meaning: * As an English surname, from the noun dore (“kind of bumblebee”). * Also as an English surname, from the placename Dorr in Derbyshire or Herefordshire; see Dorr. Sometimes influenced or directly from the noun door. * As an Irish surname, from Ó Doghair (“descendant of Doghar”), a byname meaning "sadness" (compare dubhghrá, from dubh + grá). * As a French surname, from Old French doré (“golden”). Compare Dorais.
entries.note: A diminutive of the male given name Isidore.

entries.meaning: From Dora + -een.
entries.note: A female given name.

entries.meaning: Constructed like the French Doriens. From the Latin root of Dōres + -ian. Compare Ancient Greek Δωριεύς (Dōrieús, “of Doris”).
entries.note: A male given name from Ancient Greek, famously used by Oscar Wilde in his novel The Picture of Dorian Gray (1891).

entries.meaning: Borrowed from Romanian Dorin.
entries.note: A male given name from Romanian

entries.meaning: An 18th-century coinage from Dora or Dorothy, + -inda.
entries.note: A female given name from Ancient Greek.

entries.meaning: From Ancient Greek Δωρίς (Dōrís). Etymology 1 sense 7 is owing to similarity to Boris.
entries.note: A female given name from Ancient Greek, taken to regular use at the end of the 19th century.

entries.meaning: See Dorothy.
entries.note: A female given name from Ancient Greek, a Latinate variant of Dorothy.

entries.meaning: Borrowed from Latin Dorotheus, from Ancient Greek Δωρόθεος (Dōrótheos), from δῶρον (dôron, “gift”) + θεός (theós, “God”).

entries.meaning: From Dot + -ie.
entries.note: A diminutive of the female given name Dorothy, also spelled Dotty, and sometimes also used as a formal given name.

entries.meaning: Clipping of Douglas.
entries.note: A diminutive of the male given name Douglas.

entries.meaning: Anglicized form of Scottish Gaelic Dùghall, from Old Irish dubgall (“Dane, black-haired foreigner”), synchronically from dubh (“black”) + gall (“stranger”).
entries.note: A male given name from Scottish Gaelic.

entries.meaning: From Doug + -ie.
entries.note: A diminutive of the male given names Douglas, Dougal, and Doug.

entries.meaning: From a place name, Scottish Gaelic dubh (“black”) + glais (“stream”).

entries.meaning: From Doug + -o.
entries.note: A nickname of the given name Douglas.

entries.meaning: Hebrew דוב (dov, “bear”)
entries.note: A male given name of Hebrew usage.

entries.meaning: Variant of Daw from David or daw, and of Duff from Scottish Gaelic.

entries.meaning: Variant of Dow.

entries.meaning: Borrowed from Latin Dracō, itself a borrowing from Ancient Greek Δρᾰ́κων (Drắkōn). Doublet of Dracon, dracone, dragon, and dragoon.
entries.note: A male given name from Ancient Greek or Latin.

entries.meaning: * As an English surname, from both senses of the noun drake meaning "male duck" and "dragon." * As a German surname, from Low German drake (“dragon”), related to the above. * As a Dutch surname, Americanized/West Flemish variant of Draak, also related to the above.
entries.note: A male given name transferred from the surname.

entries.meaning: A Hellenized spelling of Draco. Compare Drakon, from Ancient Greek Δρᾰ́κων (Drắkōn).
entries.note: A male given name, variant of Draco.

entries.meaning: From any of the above.

entries.meaning: From Hebrew דְּרוֹר (d'rór, “Dror, freedom, sparrow”).

entries.meaning: Borrowed from Latin Drūsilla, feminine diminutive form of the cognomen Drūsus.
entries.note: A female given name from Latin.

entries.meaning: Transliteration of Punjabi ਦੂਆ (dūā) for the Indian surname.
entries.note: A female given name from Albanian.

entries.meaning: Anglicized form of the Irish name Dubhán (from Primitive Irish ᚇᚑᚃᚐᚌᚅᚔ (dovagni)), from dubh (“black, dark”); or transferred from the surname, which is from Irish Ó Dubháin (literally “descendant of Dubhán”).
entries.note: A male given name transferred from the surname.

entries.meaning: From Old English, literally "wood or clearing of Dudda (a personal name of unknown meaning)".
entries.note: A male given name transferred from the surname, of 19th century and later usage.

entries.meaning: From the Irish and Scottish Gaelic surname, from dubh (“dark”).

entries.meaning: From Spanish Dulce.

entries.meaning: From Latin dulcis (“sweet”) in the 19th century, probably inspired by earlier names like Dowsabel and Spanish Dulcinea.
entries.note: A female given name from Latin.

entries.meaning: Clipping of Duncan.
entries.note: A diminutive of the male given name Duncan.

entries.meaning: * As a Scottish Gaelic and Irish surname, from Donnchadh, a name composed of donn (“brown”) + cath (“battle”). Also spelled as Donagh and Donaghue, Donahue. * Also as an Irish surname, Anglicized from Ó Duinnchinn, from donn (“brown”) + ceann (“head”).
entries.note: A male given name from Scottish Gaelic anglicized from Scottish Gaelic Donnchadh; the name of two early saints and of two kings of Scotland.
entries.origin: Scottish Gaelic anglicized from Scottish Gaelic Donnchadh

entries.meaning: Borrowed from Vietnamese Dung.

entries.meaning: From Duncan + -y.

entries.meaning: Borrowed from French Dupont, meaning "of the bridge".

entries.meaning: Borrowed from Sanskrit दुर्गा (durgā).

entries.meaning: Borrowed from Sanskrit दुष्यन्त (duṣyanta).

entries.meaning: Borrowed from Sanskrit दुष्यन्त (duṣyanta).
entries.note: A male given name from Sanskrit used in India.

entries.meaning: Derived from Dustin.

entries.meaning: PIE word *tewtéh₂ From Middle English Duch (“German, Low German, Dutch”), from Middle Low German dütsch, düdesch (“German, Low German, Dutch”) and Middle Dutch dūtsch, dūtsc (“German, Low German, Dutch”), from Proto-West Germanic *þiudisk, from Proto-Germanic *þiudiskaz (“of one’s people”), derived from *þeudō (“people”), from Proto-Indo-European *tewtéh₂. Doublet of Deutsch and Doitsu.

entries.meaning: From Welsh mythology; possibly from Celtic for "son of the sea" or "born from the ocean." Unrelated to the name Dillon, although the homophony may result in the two being considered variant spellings of the same name.
entries.note: A male given name from Welsh.

entries.meaning: Borrowed from Hindi [Term?], meaning halo, radiance and brightness.
entries.note: A female given name from India.

entries.meaning: From Russian Джохар (Džoxar), from Chechen Джовхӏар (Džovhar), from Arabic جَوْهَر (jawhar), from Classical Persian گوهر (gawhar).
entries.note: A male given name from Russian [in turn from Chechen].

entries.meaning: Borrowed from French Désirée (“desired”).
entries.note: A female given name from French.
